jobs.description: Who we areWorldline helps businesses of all shapes and sizes to accelerate their growth journey - quickly, simply, and securely. We are the innovators at the heart of the payments technology industry, shaping how the world pays and gets paid. Our technology powers the growth of millions of businesses across 5 continents. And just as we help our customers accelerate their business, we are committed to helping our people accelerate their careers. Together, we shape the evolution.The opportunityJoin our WLP FO expert development team within the Core Acquiring Tribe at Worldline, where you'll serve as a recognized domain expert for a specific area of the Worldline Pay Front Office authorization and switching systems. authorization — requiring you to act as the go-to authority within your domain, a best-practices resource for the team, and a trusted bridge between business requirements and technical implementation.Day-to-day responsibilities- Serve as the recognized expert within your specific WLP FO domain — guiding teams and stakeholders through complex technical and business challenges, and electronic payment processing and authorization, championing best practices and technical quality- Interpret complex business requirements within your domain and translate them into innovative, scalable technical solutions — proactively identifying risks, gaps, and opportunities, and escalating cross-domain implications to the WLP FO Architects where appropriate- Define and own technical solutions and requirements for new WLP FO functionality within your scope, recommending best practices and driving alignment across product management, software architecture, and key stakeholders- Champion the conceptual and technical integrity of payment authorization features within your domain, leading technical reviews and contributing to quality standards across the wider expert team- Guide and formally mentor junior and mid-level team members on complex technical and business challenges within your domain, serving as the best-practices and quality resource- Lead functional teams or projects within your WLP FO domain, coordinating cross-functional efforts and ensuring alignment with broader organizational objectives in collaboration with the WLP FO ArchitectsWho are we looking forWe look for big thinkers. People who can drive positive change, step up and show what's next – people with passion, can-do attitude and a hunger to learn and grow. Here you'll work with ambitious colleagues from around the world, take on unique challenges as a team, and make a real impact on the society. With an empowering culture, strong technology and extensive training opportunities, we help you accelerate your career - wherever you decide to go. Join our global team of 18,000 innovators and shape a tomorrow that is yours to own. Learn more about life at Worldline at jobs.worldline.comWe are proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. jobs.occupation: Doctoral researcher (m/f/d/x) in microbial systems biophysics (Biophysiker/in)
jobs.description: Founded in 1409, Leipzig University is one of Germany’s largest universities and a leader in research and medical training. With around 30,000 students and more than 5000 members of staff across 14 faculties, it is at the heart of the vibrant and outward-looking city of Leipzig. Leipzig University offers an innovative and international working environment as well as an exciting range of career opportunities in research, teaching, knowledge and technology transfer, infrastructure and administration.The Division of Systems Biophysics of Microbial Dynamics at the Peter Debye Institute for Soft Matter Physics at the Faculty of Physics and Earth System Sciences, seeks to fill the above position.About the position- Salary group 13 TV-L - Fixed-term position in accordance with the training plan, initially for 1 year; an extension of the fixed-term contract is planned- 50 % of a full-time position- As soon as possibleThe newly formed Division of Systems Biophysics of Microbial Dynamics (https://home.uni-leipzig.de/sysbiophys/) , led by Professor Katja Taute, is part of the Peter Debye Institute for Soft Matter Physics (https://www.physes.uni-leipzig.de/en/pdi) , which hosts a broad range of biophysics research. Active matter, including bacterial systems, is a growing key research area at the Institute. Our research group develops and uses biophysical methods, including high-throughput, 3D bacterial tracking and microfluidics, in combination with theory and simulations, to quantitatively analyse the spatio-temporal dynamics of bacteria at the level of individuals and populations. One research focus is the chemotactic navigation of bacteria in mechanically complex environments. In nature, swimming bacteria navigate relative to chemical stimuli in environments ranging from open waters to soil and the gut.The new doctoral researcher is to investigate how the gut bacterium E. coli navigates mechanically complex environments that mimic properties of its natural habitat. Properties of both the bacteria and the environment will be modulated in a controlled fashion to identify the underlying physical mechanisms and address the following questions:- What is the relationship between behavioural and material parameters that enable optimal navigation?- Is optimal intracellular information processing specific to the type of environment?- How do bacteria navigate mechanical gradients?The role- Independent, original, experimental scientific research on the above project- Additional scientific qualification (preparing a doctoral thesis)- Thorough documentation of research- Publication of research results, for example at conferences, workshops, or in scientific articles- Contributions to the Institute’s teaching responsibilitiesAbout you- An excellent scientific university degree (master of science or comparable) in (bio-)physics, (bio-)engineering or a related field- Very good command of at least one programming language (Matlab or Python preferred) and of quantitative scientific data analysis- A track record of academic excellence (e.g. very good grades in the course of study, research or study scholarships and prizes, scientific publications)- Written and spoken professional fluency in English (at least equivalent to level B2)- Excellent written communication skills, demonstrated through coherent, structured and precise writing- Experience with microscopy and scientific image processing would be an advantage- Interest in quantitative experimental interdisciplinary science- Collaborative mindset and teamwork skillsWhat we offer you- a varied role with a high degree of responsibility in the dynamic environment of a major university- a professional English-language work environment at the leading edge of interdisciplinary science- Collaboration in a friendly, supportive and motivated team- flexible working hours and mobile working to support work-life balance- Goal-oriented staff development throughout your working life, with opportunities for continuing professional development- a wide range of occupational health management services - Remuneration in line with the collective bargaining agreement of the federal states (TV-L), including an annual special payment and occupational pension scheme- excellent transport links and the option to purchase a discounted public transport ticket, such as the Deutschlandticket as a commuter pass- a wide range of food options in the refectories and cafés operated by Studentenwerk Leipzig.Leipzig University aims to increase the proportion of women in positions of responsibility and therefore expressly invites qualified women to apply. Severely disabled persons – or persons deemed legally equal to them under Book IX of the German Social Code – are encouraged to apply and will be given preference in the case of equal suitability. If you have any questions about accessibility or need assistance with this application process, please contact Leipzig University’s disability officers at: schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de (https://mailto:schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de) .Have we sparked your interest?Please submit your application in English addressed to Fakultät für Physik und Erdsystemwissenschaften, Herrn Dekan Professor Dr. Johannes Quaas by 1 November 2026 via our online application portal.Please include the following documents with your application:- A short letter of motivation (max. 1 page) in which you clearly explain why you would like to work on this project- A scientific CV (evidence of creative and independent scientific work is an advantage)- The names and contact information of two people who have agreed to provide academic references- Academic transcripts clearly listing the courses taken and grades achieved in your entire scientific higher education (bachelor’s as well as master’s or comparable degrees)

TUD Dresden University of Technology, as a University of Excellence, is one of the leading and most dynamic research institutions in the country. For TUD diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.At the Faculty of Chemistry and Food Chemistry, the Chair of Inorganic Chemistry I offers, subject to the availability of resources, a project position asResearch Associate / PostDoc (m/f/x)(subject to personal qualification, employees are remunerated according to salary group E 13 TV-L)starting January 1, 2027. The position is limited until February 29, 2028. The period of employment is governed by § 2 (2) Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz-WissZeitVG).Tasks:The candidate will be in charge of developing a novel generation of computing architectures based on ion computing. Development of novel switchable ultracapacitors and microsupercapacitors for iontronic applications, synthesis of porous carbon materials and porous membranes, development and adaption of new electrolyte formulations, electrochemical characterization, impedance spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry, integration into a team of PhD and master students, scientific publishing, data management.Requirements: - very good university and PhD degree in chemistry or materials science- experience in the field of electrochemistry in particular ultracapacitors, cyclovoltammetry, impedance spectroscopy- broad knowledge of materials characterization methods in particular as relevant for porous materials- able to work in an international team and to guide a team- high self-motivation- good command of written and spoken English- good PC skills- capacity for teamwork and organizational talentTUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. We therefore expressly encourage women to apply. The university is a family-friendly university. We welcome applications from candidates with disabilities. If multiple candidates prove to be equally qualified, those with disabilities or with equivalent status pursuant to the German Social Code IX (SGB IX) will receive priority for employment.Application:Please submit your detailed application with the usual documents by October 26, 2026 (stamped arrival date of the university central mail service or the time stamp on the email server of TUD applies), preferably via the TUD SecureMail Portal https://securemail.tu-dresden.de by sending it as a single pdf file to sekretariat-ac1@mailbox.tu-dresden.de (https://mailto:sekretariat-ac1@mailbox.tu-dresden.de) or to:TU Dresden, Chair of Inorganic Chemistry I, Frau Linda Petersohn, Helmholtzstr. 10,01069 Dresden, Germany.Please submit copies only, as your application will not be returned to you. Expenses incurred in attending interviews cannot be reimbursed.TUD is a founding partner in the DRESDEN-concept alliance.Reference to data protection: Your data protection rights, the purpose for which your data will be processed, as well as further information about data protection is available to you on the website: https://tu-dresden.de/karriere/datenschutzhinweis (https://tu-dresden.de/karriere/datenschutzhinweis) .Ergänzende Informationen:Anforderungen an den Bewerber: Grundkenntnisse: Elektrochemie

jobs.occupation: IMPACT EVALUATION, RESEARCH, AND LEARNING MANAGER (Maternity cover) (Fachangestellte/r - Markt- und Sozialforschung)
jobs.description: OVERVIEWFairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.Unit’s description and purpose: The Global Impact unit strengthens the Fairtrade system by driving institutional learning and effectiveness through robust monitoring and evaluation systems. We are the hub for the analysis and communication of high-quality data and information about Fairtrade and its impact, as well as supporting strategy delivery. The unit includes the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) team, which is the Fairtrade system’s hub for MEL which directly connects evidence to strategic decision for the Global Strategy, individual Fairtrade projects and global programmes, Standards, producer support, and more.PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIESOverseeing Fairtrade Research and Evaluation: Manages Global Impact commissioned research and evaluations, and supports research and evaluations commissioned by other Fairtrade International units and Fairtrade organizations, ensuring that there are rigorous research methodologies, effective dissemination of findings, practical recommendations, and actionable learnings for the Fairtrade system. Develops and implements procedures and guidelines for the management of research and evaluations within the Fairtrade system.Amplifying research findings internally and externally: Organizes learning events based on research to ensure learnings are promoted and used by various stakeholder groups within the Fairtrade system. Helps to build appropriate action-plans based on research where learnings are used to promote adaptation, change, and improvement. Presents Fairtrade research findings at external research workshops and conventions and helps to organize and facilitate presentations of others in the Fairtrade system. Encouraging a Fairtrade Learning Culture: Develops a Fairtrade Learning Strategy and adapts/maintains Fairtrade Research for Learning Agenda. Ensures that Fairtrade research contributes to understanding Fairtrade’s impact and tests the assumptions in Fairtrade’s Theory of Change. Coordinates research efforts across the Fairtrade system through the Research Task Force. Hosts and guides occasional research-focused interns, students from partner organisations, or student assistants.Building External Research Collaborations: Builds on an existing academic engagement strategy to engage with external research institutions more deeply to collaboratively fund and perform research on Fairtrade’s impact. Brainstorms with external research teams, contributes to research funding proposals, builds research methodologies, jointly oversees research implementation, and works together to interpret, amplify, and communicate findings.Managing Digital Learning Platforms: Acts as the product owner for Fairtrade’s Research Hub, a searchable database and platform of external studies exploring Fairtrade’s impact, and Fairlearn, a platform for live and asynchronous Fairtrade e-learning. Contributes to a Steering Committee for an Impact Platform for understanding and learning from Fairtrade’s projects, programmes, and commissioned studies.Other tasks that are consistent with the level and responsibilities of this post.SKILLS REQUIREDLevel of education: The position holder will have a Master’s degree (With a research component) or higher (PhD preferred) in development economics, econometrics, applied sociology, social sciences or another relevant field in management or natural sciences. Years of professional experience: A minimum of five years’ experience in research and/or impact evaluations, with at least two years’ experience working on topics relevant to, or with, stakeholders from the Global South.Job Specific Competencies/knowledge:- Project Management- Research and Evaluation- International Development Expertise- Stakeholder Management- Enhancing data-driven decision making- eLearning Content- Event/conferences organization- Capacity BuildingPersonal Qualities: - Cross-cultural communication- Facilitation- Rapid Learning- Collaboration/Teamwork- Problem Solving- Multitasking- Teaching- Presentation Skills- Relationship Management- Evidence Collecting- Flexibility- MentoringSoftware/Tools:- Microsoft 365 (Excel, Word, Outlook, Powerpoint, Teams, Planner, Clipchamp)- Adobe Creative Cloud & Suite- Miro- Canva- Claude.ai, or similar AI assistant toolsTERMS AND CONDITIONS- This is a full-time, maternity cover (apprx. until March 2028) position within Fairtrade International.- Location is at Fairtrade International offices in Bonn, Germany with the opportunity for hybrid work arrangements- The office language is English.- Salary as per the Collective Bargaining Agreement for the Wholesale and Foreign Trade Industries for North Rhine Westphalia Group 6a and over tariff payments (starting from 5455,00 Euros gross per month)- Holiday Bonus and 13th salary  - 30 days of holidays per year (for full time employees)- Subsidised public transportation ticket- Subsidised meal services- Childcare cost subsidy Please note that Fairtrade International is strict on compliance with the required qualification criteria mentioned above, and only those candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

We are looking for a highly motivated and proactive Supplier Quality Manager (Europe) (d/f/m) at our site in Hemer or Düsseldorf to establish and maintain a robust quality ecosystem across our European supplier base. This role requires a strategic mindset to drive supplier quality improvements, mitigate risks, and ensure compliance with LIXIL standards and processes. The ideal candidate will have strong cross-functional collaboration skills and a passion for innovation in quality management. Key responsibilities and main challenges:·         Implement advanced supplier quality control processes to enhance supplier performance and achieve key performance indicators (KPIs).·         Develop preventive risk mitigation processes using APQP methodologies and predictive analytics.·         Support key suppliers in establishing quality firewalls through periodic training and continuous improvement initiatives.·         Assist the sourcing team in supplier selection and evaluation through audits and performance monitoring.·         Conduct supplier audits based on VDA6.1 and VDA6.3.·         Collaborate with the regional quality team on new product development quality, focusing on PPAP/ISIR verification.·         Analyze supplier quality issues and drive corrective actions using 8D, 5-Why, and APDCA methodologies.·         Continuously monitor and improve supplier quality performance.·         Validate key supplier laboratories according to specifications and standards.·         Lead competency development and internal training for the European SQM team.
